_readme: One list of every future feature and tab. The Coming soon page and the Lab status board both read it, so they cannot disagree. A feature's tier (live / tested / untested) and place come from roadmap_page.py; this file adds the workflow it belongs to, when it is planned, whether it needs AI, who it helps, a one-line purpose and a link to its evidence card. The order (now / next / later) is a proposal for review, not a promise.

workflows.label: Finding cases
workflows.blurb: Ways to locate the right decisions.

workflows.label: Reading a case
workflows.blurb: What a decision says, laid out so it is quick to read.

workflows.label: Analysing your own draft
workflows.blurb: Putting your own memo or draft against the case law.

workflows.label: Citations and statutes
workflows.blurb: Finding, linking and checking the authorities a decision relies on.

workflows.label: Court files and teamwork
workflows.blurb: Following live files and working with colleagues.

workflows.label: The library itself
workflows.blurb: Making what is already in the library more correct and more complete.

workflows.label: Ready for the agency
workflows.blurb: What an approval and a deployment inside the agency would need.

horizons.label: Next
horizons.blurb: Built or being built; proposed to go live next.

horizons.label: Later
horizons.blurb: Decided or imagined; not built yet.

ai.label: Needs a local model
ai.blurb: Would run only on computers the agency controls.

passage-search.purpose: Type a sentence, get the paragraphs that say it, with no AI.

themes.purpose: Group the arguments that keep coming up across decisions.

fingerprints.purpose: Describe a decision by its tags and citations to find similar ones.

embeddings.purpose: Search by meaning, not just words. Paused until it measures better.

decision-maker-insights.purpose: See how a judge or Board member has ruled on an issue.

case-at-a-glance.purpose: A small card on top of a decision: parties, subject, issues, arguments, built once at intake.

discussion-units.purpose: Split a decision into facts, issues, reasoning and outcome.

whose-position.purpose: Show whose argument each paragraph is dealing with.

show-your-work.purpose: Show how each label or link was worked out, beside the label.

argument-identification.purpose: List the cases and statutes in your memo with paragraph links; spotting its arguments needs a local model.

memo-check.purpose: Check the authorities a memo cites and what treatment each got.

deidentify.purpose: Remove names and identifiers before a decision or memo is shared.

institutional-memory.purpose: Search the Division's earlier positions and what persuaded members.

citation-extraction.purpose: Find every citation in a decision and link it to the case.

citation-resolving.purpose: Decide which case a citation means and land on the right paragraph.

citation-treatment.purpose: See whether later decisions followed, distinguished or doubted a case.

citation-enhancements.purpose: A one-line plain reason beside each citing paragraph.

neighbourhoods.purpose: From one case, see what it relies on and what cites it.

authority-trends.purpose: Sort authorities into emerging, dominant and fading.

statute-references.purpose: Link the sections of the Act and Regulations a decision cites.

laws-regulations.purpose: Add more statutes, regulations and guidance to the reference library.

fc-analytics.purpose: Charts of how Federal Court immigration files progress and end.

fc-follow.purpose: Follow a list of file numbers and see what is new on each.

fc-deadlines.purpose: Attach a deadline to a file and see what is due.

fc-collection.purpose: Collect new entries on the Court's record automatically.

fc-record.purpose: Read more of the Court's free-text record with fixed rules.

alerts.purpose: Save a search and get a short list of new matching decisions.

accounts.purpose: Sign in as yourself and keep your saved work.

teams.purpose: Shared folders of cases, searches and notes for a team.

annotations.purpose: Highlight a passage and add a note, private or shared.

export.purpose: Turn a folder into a Word or CSV case list or short brief.

history.purpose: A record of what was searched, opened and noted, by whom.

case-types.purpose: Label each decision by kind, such as a judicial review.

outcome-coding.purpose: Record who won, from the ruling text, by fixed rules.

parties.purpose: Tidy the many spellings of the Minister and party names.

judges.purpose: Tidy judge and Board member names into one person each.

measuring.purpose: Give every automated step a measured accuracy number.

more-cases.purpose: Add more courts and tribunals, such as the Refugee Appeal Division.

more-tags.purpose: Add more tags for issues and grounds, such as inadmissibility.

daily-intake.purpose: Add new decisions every day without anyone running a script.

id-iad.purpose: Add Immigration Division and Appeal Division decisions.

review-pack.purpose: Plain documents a security or privacy reviewer would ask for.

public-only.purpose: One switch that makes a public-law-only version of the site.

hosting.purpose: Where the site and any model would run for the agency.

backups.purpose: Regular database copies and a tested way to restore them.

accessibility.purpose: Meet the government web accessibility standard.

french-ui.purpose: Every label and page available in French.

hardening.purpose: Standard protections for a government web service.

internal-documents.purpose: Search the agency's own briefs and memos beside public decisions.

agency-repositories.purpose: Add the agency's private decisions and files to the library.

handling-marks.purpose: Show where each result came from and how it must be handled.

on-prem-model.purpose: A language model on agency computers, used only for optional features.

data-safety.purpose: Show where each document is stored and who can read it.

stored-as-data.purpose: Any AI work runs once when a decision is added and is stored as data.

human-review.purpose: No AI-written label is shown until a sample has been reviewed by a person.
